A federal judge, Mark Pittman, is seeking to learn about any agreement that may have led to a Musk-owned company dropping its antitrust allegations against Apple. Here are the details.

Judge orders production of any deal made with Apple

Earlier this week, X and SpaceXAI filed a motion with the court asking to voluntarily drop their claims against Apple and have the case permanently closed. The lawsuit was filed by the two companies against Apple and OpenAI last year.

According to the initial lawsuit documents, Apple and OpenAI were alleged to have conspired to block competing AI apps from gaining visibility on the App Store through an agreement to integrate ChatGPT into Siri and Apple Intelligence. Both Apple and OpenAI have denied the allegations.

In the motion filed earlier this week, X and SpaceXAI only said they had "reached a settlement on the claims against Apple in this lawsuit," and emphasised they were not seeking to drop the claims against OpenAI.

As POLITICO first reported, Judge Mark Pittman, who is presiding over the case, has ordered X and SpaceXAI to submit to the court "any agreement or series of agreements made with Apple to resolve the plaintiffs' claims against Apple in this lawsuit."

The order comes in response to an emergency motion filed by OpenAI. OpenAI asked the court to force X and SpaceXAI to disclose their settlement agreement with Apple. Pittman also ordered the companies to respond to OpenAI's motion by noon on September 17.
